clusters.state_of_play: A Fox News poll shows Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley by 9 points in the North Carolina Senate race, with Democrats holding an enthusiasm edge over Republicans. Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has selected former Republican Mayor John Giles, now independent, as her running mate. In Minnesota, progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic Senate primary by 20 points over moderate Rep. Angie Craig, in a race defined by anti-ICE anger following the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. Flanagan, backed by Bernie Sanders and Ilhan Omar, could become the first Native woman in the Senate. Her win is the latest in a series of progressive victories over moderates in the Midwest — including Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan U.S. Senate primary win the prior week — and marks a second straight primary setback for Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer. Flanagan faces baggage from a Minnesota fraud scandal that occurred during her tenure as Lt. Gov. Former TV sports reporter Michele Tafoya won the Republican Senate primary in Minnesota and will face Flanagan in November. Minnesota is the first state to set all-female matchups in both its biggest races: Flanagan vs. Tafoya for Senate, and Klobuchar vs. Demuth for governor. Ilhan Omar has been projected to win the Democratic primary in Minnesota's 5th Congressional District. Sen. Amy Klobuchar has been projected to win the Minnesota DFL gubernatorial primary and will face Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth in November; Demuth defeated Trump-backed MyPillow founder Mike Lindell, who received roughly 31% of the vote, losing by about 11 points (over 45,000 votes). Lindell has requested a recount and says he will pay nearly $1 million for the hand recount, since Minnesota only funds automatic recounts when the margin is under 0.25%. In Minnesota's 1st Congressional District, GOP incumbent Brad Finstad survived a primary against challengers Gregory Goetzman and Oliver Morlan. In Connecticut, former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin has been projected to defeat veteran Democratic incumbent Rep. John Larson in the House primary. Larson's loss makes him the 10th House incumbent to lose a primary this cycle, an unusually high figure driven by Democrats pushing leaders to pass the torch to a younger, more progressive generation and Republicans reckoning with Trump's influence. In Wisconsin, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley defeated democratic socialist Francesca Hong in a stunningly narrow Democratic gubernatorial primary — winning by less than a percentage point — after re-entering the race and securing an endorsement from outgoing Gov. Tony Evers, who called Crowley 'the future of the party.' Crowley, who could become the state's first Black governor, will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany in November. Following her loss, Hong endorsed Crowley. Sabato's Crystal Ball subsequently shifted the Wisconsin governor's race toward Democrats. In South Carolina's special GOP Senate race, Darline Graham (32.6%) and Rep. Ralph Norman (24%) emerged from the Aug. 11 primary to advance to an Aug. 25 runoff, with Rep. Russell Fry finishing third at 20.3%. Trump-backed Graham denied being a 'nepo senator.' Ahead of the runoff, Graham and Norman debated at the Newberry Opera House on Aug. 18, 2026, where Graham admitted 'national security is not my thing' and, per fuller reporting, said 'I'm just going to be honest here... not that informed on national security, so - but I do support the military,' drawing gasps and boos from the crowd, while Norman blasted Senate GOP leaders' five-week recess as 'a slap in the face' amid the stalled SAVE Act. The debate flub sparked widespread criticism, including from MAGA podcaster Megyn Kelly, who called Graham's answer 'disqualifying,' and prompted President Trump to schedule an Aug. 21 campaign rally for Graham in Myrtle Beach ahead of the runoff. The two-week runoff campaign has been described as a 'slugfest'; Trump's super PAC has spent heavily to bolster Graham, though some Republicans reportedly expect her to lose to Norman in the Aug. 25 runoff. Ahead of the runoff vote, polling showed a tight or Norman-leaning race, but prediction market Kalshi still gave Graham a 70% chance of winning as of Tuesday afternoon, up from 67% Monday night, and the contest was drawing unusually high turnout for what is typically a sleepy runoff, prompting national framing of the race as a test of Trump's political influence. Sabato's Crystal Ball's Kyle Kondik has analyzed GOP efforts to use Trump's endorsement to energize the party's base for the runoff and broader midterms. Trump's endorsements have broadly flopped in major statewide governor races: in addition to Lindell, Trump-backed Andy Ogles (TN) and Amir Hassan (MI) also lost their primaries; Hassan lost to Thomas Smith. An analysis by G. Elliott Morris found that primary election polls miss by an average of 13 points, and prediction markets were also shown to have failed on the Hong result in Wisconsin. El-Sayed's historic nomination as the first Muslim nominated by a major party for U.S. Senate has triggered anti-Muslim vitriol on multiple fronts, tempering elation among Muslim Americans. El-Sayed also faces a significant fundraising challenge in the general election, with Sanders expected to need to provide more active support to shepherd him through November. El-Sayed has also publicly distanced himself from progressive commentator Hasan Piker's remarks on Israel and Jewish Americans.
